questions.question_text:
A trapezium-shaped hole lies entirely inside a trapezium-shaped panel. The panel has parallel sides of $20\text{ m}$ and $14\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $8\text{ m}$. The hole has parallel sides of $9\text{ m}$ and $5\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $4\text{ m}$.
Find the area of the panel that remains, in square metres.

options.why: Added the hole's area of $28\text{ m}^2$ to the panel's area of $136\text{ m}^2$ instead of subtracting it.
Left out the halving for the hole, subtracting $4(9+5)=56\text{ m}^2$ instead of $28\text{ m}^2$.
Gave the area of the hole instead of the area of the panel that remains.
Added the rhombus instead of subtracting the hole punched out of the label.
Left out the halving for the kite only, using $12\times18=216$ for the outer shape.
Left out the halving in both diagonal formulas, using $216-30$.

questions.question_text:
A sign consists of a central square with an isosceles triangle joined externally along each of its left and right sides. The square has side length $6.5\text{ m}$. The two outer triangle tips lie on the horizontal line through the centre of the square and are $21.5\text{ m}$ apart.
Find the total area of the sign, in square metres.

options.why: Used the full width of $21.5\text{ m}$ as the sum of the triangle heights instead of subtracting the square's width, giving $42.25+\frac{6.5\times21.5}{2}=112.125$.
Left out the halving for the triangles, giving $42.25+6.5\times15=139.75$.
Found the combined area of the triangles but left out the square's area of $42.25\text{ m}^2$.

questions.solution_text:
The two triangles' perpendicular heights add to $21.5-6.5=15\text{ m}$.
$A_1=6.5\times6.5$
$=42.25\text{ m}^2$
$A_2+A_3=\frac{6.5\times15}{2}$
$=48.75\text{ m}^2$
$A_{\text{Total}}=42.25+48.75$
$=91\text{ m}^2$
